summary: The team is in execution mode on two fronts: launching the Intelligent China webpage this week to anchor the China-first SEO/AI-search push, and finalizing the knowledge website redesign while clearing a lingering Outlook lockout.
summaryDetail: The single most important thing right now is getting the Intelligent China webpage live this week, the first concrete step in a strategic pivot that prioritizes Asia Star and Intelligent China over US partnerships for search visibility. That visibility work needs Joseph's target-area and audience brief plus a CRM analysis of Asia Star participants to move forward, and the Google Ads conversion tracking setup still needs documentation and an audit. In parallel, the knowledge website redesign is nearing a decision: the team favors the current homepage with better menu categorization and editorial-style article surfacing, so Joseph must share the HTML concept, the team must hold a 30-minute feedback session, and Joker must then implement changes. Urgent housekeeping this week is resolving the Outlook account lockout by deleting and re-adding accounts with the new password across all devices and confirming the backend unlock with CKGSB. Looking ahead, the 2026 Women in Leadership Forum is building momentum with Ms. Kanta Singh confirmed and Ira Zaka revising the ESG and Social Innovation Report to be more program-focused; other upcoming items include the CKGSB x European Chamber Shanghai event on November 13, sales pushes for the Stanford and CES programs, and the anniversary infographic update.
